text: I have noted the MRI findings showing multifocal demyelinating lesions suggestive of PML, and the finger-to-nose test confirms ataxia. Since your deep tendon reflexes are pending, could you tell me if you have any history of immunosuppression, HIV, or recent chemotherapy? Also, do you experience any sensory changes like numbness or tingling in your extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without contrast enhancement are classic for PML, which is an opportunistic infection of the white matter typically caused by the JC virus in immunocompromised individuals. While you have no recent fever, your significant medical history and the specific MRI pattern strongly support this diagnosis over multiple sclerosis. Given the high risk of rapid progression, we must immediately assess your immune status.

REQUEST TEST: HIV Test (ELISA/Western Blot) and CD4 Count.
